To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the light yields of SNO+ scintillator and EJ- 301 scintillator become non-linear below electron energies of ∼ 0. 4 MeV.

the response of linear alkyl benzene (LAB) based and EJ- 301 scintillator with respect to electrons become non-linear below ∣ 0.4 MeV and that the non-linearities are due to Cherenkov light re-absorption and re-emission in the scintillator.
the energy scale of the SNO+ scintillator linearizes at ∼ 0. 4 MeV and is non-linear below this energy, and that the energy scale linearizes at ∷ 0. 3 MeV for EJ-301.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new scintillation-based detectors for the measurement of low-energy electrons.
the study of the scintillation light yield as a function of the electron energy in the energy region below 1 MeV.
the measurement of the energy dependence of the scintillation light yields of linear-alkylbenzene (LAB) and EJ-30 1 liquid scintillators in the energy range from 0.09 to 3.00 MeV.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SNO+ light yield scale is linear with respect to electrons in the energy region 0.4–3.2 MeV.
the SNO+ light yield is linear with respect to electrons above ∼ 0. 4 MeV, but is non-linear below ∝ 0. 5 MeV.
the light yield of linear alkyl benzene scintillators in SNO+ is linear with respect to electron energies in the range 0.4–3 Me V.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for electron energy measurements in the range 0.1–3 MeV, the EJ-301 detector is preferable to the SNO+ detector.
we have demonstrated that the response of linear alkyl benzene-based scintillators to electrons is non-linear below ∝ 0.4 MeV and that the EJ-301 response is linear to ∝ 0
the light yields of the two scintillators are linear with energy above 0.4 MeV, with an average energy resolution for the two detectors of ∼ 10 %.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a linear response to electrons is not a sufficient condition to guarantee a linear response to nuclear recoils.
a linear energy response for electrons is not expected below ∼ 1 MeV for any scintillator.
the light yield of both scintillators is not linear with respect to the electron energy.
